sentences.text: Sneathia are urogenital anaerobes, and two species have been identified: Sneathia vaginalis and Sneathia sanguinegens.
A comparative genomic analysis of 12 Sneathia genomes reported small genomes of 1.25 to 1.35 Mbp with low GC content, encoding glycogen utilization and lactic and mixed acid fermentation.
That analysis also reported core and accessory virulence factors in Sneathia genomes, including an exotoxin, additional hemolysins and adhesins.
Sneathia species have been described as emerging pathogens associated with bacterial vaginosis, preterm birth, chorioamnionitis, non-gonococcal urethritis and HPV-mediated cervical carcinogenesis.
A systematic review and meta-analysis of 17 observational studies reported Sneathia to be more abundant in patients with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and cervical cancer.
